title: Potato Salad with Egg and Fat‑Free Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: A salad made from boiled potatoes, hard‑boiled eggs and any fat‑free dressing (such as mustard‑vinegar sauce, low‑fat yogurt dressing or a simple vinaigrette). It is a light, diet‑friendly dish rich in protein, B‑vitamins and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed vegetables and provide vitamin C and potassium.
Eggs are a complete source of all essential amino acids.
Fat‑free dressings keep the calorie count low while still delivering flavor through herbs, mustard and vinegar.
The salad is usually served cold, making it ideal for picnics and work lunches.
Different cultures add various herbs: dill in Russia, green onion in the US, and nori in Japan.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and potatoes together provide high‑quality animal and plant protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The absence of fat in the dressing reduces the overall energy density, helpful for weight management.

items.title: Potassium source
items.content: Potatoes supply potassium, which helps maintain fluid balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: B‑vitamin rich
items.content: Eggs are rich in vitamin B12, while potatoes provide vitamin B6, both important for nervous system function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from potatoes and added herbs promotes healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding too much salt to the dressing can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Eggs should be fully cooked to avoid salmonella.

items.title: High glycemic index of potatoes
items.content: People with diabetes should monitor portion size because potatoes raise blood glucose quickly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, a side to meat or fish, or in sandwiches. Fresh herbs (dill, parsley), green onions or a dash of mustard can enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Add the dressing just before serving to prevent the potatoes from becoming soggy.
